title: Winter and House
premise: Astrid Eriksen, a skeptical urban explorer, maps a tunnel network beneath a derelict house and discovers the mirrors inside reflect everything one second late — a lag that widens each night. The house's surviving family, the Winters, are trapped in a generational bargain: when the lag reaches ten seconds, the reflection keeps what it has learned to copy, and the originals are erased. Astrid, who has spent their life refusing to believe in anything they can't survey, must accept that the thing wearing their face in the glass is learning faster than they are. In the end, Astrid breaks the count by shattering the great mirror from behind — through the tunnel side — trading their own reflection as the anchor that holds the door shut, and walks out of the dark with the family, no longer certain which of them is the original.
about_author: G. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former municipal surveyor who spent eleven years cataloguing basements, culverts, and structures that official maps insisted did not exist. They write horror about places that keep records of the people who enter them.

chapters.title: The Unsurveyed Level
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Hired to verify a property line, Astrid finds a tunnel entrance beneath the old Winter house that appears on no map, no survey, no archive. Their instruments read fine; their gut reads wrong. The beat is professional curiosity curdling into the first honest unease they've felt in years.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Inside the house at dusk, Astrid notices the hallway mirror lags: raise a hand, watch it follow a beat behind. They test it with a lighter, a stopwatch, cold logic — and the lag is real and growing. The beat is the skeptic's worldview cracking on its own terms: measurable, repeatable, impossible.

chapters.title: The Winter Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Astrid and Mara Winter, the family matriarch. Astrid confronts the three remaining Winters — Mara, her son Dev, and his daughter Ilsa — who are not surprised by the mirror. They've been counting for generations. The beat is wary alliance forming over shared terror neither will name yet.

chapters.title: What the Glass Learns
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The child explains the rules her grandmother taught her: the reflections aren't copies, they're students, and every night the lag grows by one second because they're studying harder. Ilsa shows Astrid her own reflection mouthing words she hasn't said yet. The beat is dread refracted through innocence.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Five
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. At five seconds, the reflections begin acting independently — setting the table in the mirrored dining room, watching the family sleep through the wardrobe glass. Dev, who lost his wife to the last count, refuses to run until he understands what took her. The beat is grief weaponized into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Tunnel Logic
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid maps the tunnels properly and discovers the mirror-world has its own version of them — same tunnels, wrong geometry, and something moving through them toward the house from below. The escape route and the threat share one road. The beat is the planner realizing the map itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Eight Seconds
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With two nights left, Mara confesses the origin: her grandmother made the bargain to survive a famine winter, offering 'what we show' instead of 'what we are.' The reflections have been collecting the payment ever since. The beat is inherited guilt laid bare, and Mara's quiet decision to be the one who stays.

chapters.title: The Reflection That Waits
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Trapped overnight in the tunnels, Astrid meets their own reflection coming the other way — patient, fluent, wearing Astrid's skepticism like a borrowed coat. It offers a trade: let it out, and the family goes free. The beat is identity under siege; Astrid can't prove which one is lying, including to themselves.

chapters.title: Nine
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating fast among all four. On the penultimate night the house's mirrors merge into one continuous surface, and the reflections walk out of the walls. Dev falls protecting Ilsa; Mara holds the doorway with an heirloom hand-mirror; Astrid realizes the count can be broken only from behind the glass. The beat is sacrifice cascading into resolve.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid enters the mirror-world through the tunnel, shatters the great mirror from its far side, and anchors the breach with their own captured reflection — becoming the house's new, willing record. Dawn: the Winters walk out into snow, free but hollowed, and somewhere behind them a clean new mirror waits, reflecting nothing yet. The beat is survival purchased at identity's price, and found family carrying each other away from the count.
